tags.description: WWII Japanese coastal freighter. Bombed Operation Desecrate One March 30-31 1944; sank evening April 1 1944. Length reported as 285ft (87m) by Fish N Fins or 295ft (90m) by Wrecked In My rEvo — sources conflict. Tonnage reported 1,941 tons (Fish N Fins) or ~2,100 tons (Palau Dive Adventures) — sources conflict. Build year reported 1942 or 1943 — sources conflict. Deck at 30m, keel at 40m, forward kingpost tower at 12m. Coal-burning quadruple-expansion steam engine. Nicknamed Lionfish Wreck. Rediscovered April 1989 by Francis Toribiong and Klaus Lindemann.
tags.name: Chuyo Maru
tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-08-16: added tracesofwar.com as a 4th independent source. It reports build year 1942 (vs. 1943 per fishnfins.com) and length 295ft/90m (vs. 285ft/87m per fishnfins.com); tonnage 1,941 tons is consistent across sources. Conflicts remain unresolved across all 4 sources and are stated as a range/conflict in the description rather than picked. Sinking date (1 April 1944), Operation Desecrate One context, and 1989 rediscovery by Toribiong/Lindemann re-confirmed unchanged.

tags.name: Lighthouse Channel
tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-08-16: added zentacle.com as a 4th independent source (reviewer-aggregated dive site database), which independently confirms 16.4ft/5m max depth, beginner-level drift dive near Koror's lighthouse, boat access. Zentacle mentions occasional 'big sharks' but this is a single, low-confidence source and was not added to the description. Mandarin fish claim re-confirmed distinct from (but consistent in character with) the separately-named Mandarin Fish Lake site in Risong Bay — Lighthouse Channel is a real, independently attested site near the Koror lighthouse, not a duplicate/misnamed entry.

tags.name: Sand Bar
tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-08-16: German Channel construction date corrected. palaudiveadventures.com/german-channel-history specifies the channel was completed in 1911 by the German South Seas Phosphate Company (SAG) as part of phosphate mining operations on Angaur that ran 1909-1913 (236,087 tons extracted 1909-1913 per that source). The previous '1908-1911, blasted for phosphate transport' figure was imprecise on the year range and has been corrected in the markdown. Manta ray species (reef vs. oceanic) still not confirmed at this specific site by any source — description continues to avoid species attribution.

tags.name: The Big Drop Off
tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-08-16: shark species claim corrected. Palau Dive Adventures (big-drop-off-palau) reports nurse sharks as a third species alongside grey reef and whitetip; Fish N Fins (149-big-drop-off) instead reports leopard sharks, not nurse sharks. This is a genuine, unresolved source conflict — markdown now presents both claims explicitly as disputed rather than stating nurse sharks as a confirmed fact from a single source.

tags.name: Ngerechong North Coral Garden
tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-08-16: found a new corroborating source, Scuba Diving magazine's 'Palau's Lucky Seven' (scubadiving.com), which independently confirms this is part of a horseshoe-shaped reef ~21mi/34km SE of Koror near Denges Passage, shallow zone 0-12m, sandy sloping bottom, visibility 20-30m on incoming tide. Denges Passage cuttlefish sightings mentioned by that source are NOT attributed to this site — they are specific to the separate Denges Passage location and excluded per marine-life accuracy policy.

tags.name: Jake SeaPlane
tags.qa_notes: Re-audited 2026-08-16: re-verified via fishnfins.com and discoverwildlife.com. Depth (~12m), condition (fuselage and wing largely intact, tail section separated a few meters away), cause-of-loss uncertainty (unbent propellers suggesting non-combat loss), and 1994 discovery by a local fisherman all re-confirmed unchanged. A lower-quality tertiary source (outono.net) reported a shallower ~6m depth and a more fragmented condition, but this conflicts with our two established, more detailed sources and was not incorporated.
